cells.title: Serve principles from the hub in onboard
cells.action: D2: when `principles_on_hub(repo_root)` is true and the Claude runtime is in scope, onboard reads each `bee-principle-*` directory of the engine skills source on the hub with `hub_show` through `hub_runner(repo_root)`. When every one is `active`, the skill sync for the repo Claude target only (target kind repo-claude, `.claude/skills`) leaves every `bee-principle-*` entry out of its source list, so the existing deletion loop plans `remove_skill` for local copies. Codex, opencode, plugin and the legacy global targets are unchanged. When any principle is missing or not active, or the hub read skips, the source list is unchanged and onboard reports exactly one `skipped_skills` entry `{target: "skillstation-principles", reason}` naming the first failing id or the skip reason. D3: when `opts.skillstation` and hub mode, plan one `publish_skillstation` item per `bee-principle-*` source skill that stages from the engine source rendered for the claude runtime (the same render the Claude sync uses), not from `.claude/skills`; apply runs the existing commit-then-activate path. Without hub mode, plan and apply output are byte-identical to today; without --skillstation the hub is never written. Tests use `set_test_hub`, never the real binary: hub mode with all active plans removal of local principle folders only under .claude/skills and keeps .agents copies; one draft keeps all and gives one skip row; hub skip gives one skip row; --skillstation in hub mode plans one publish item per principle; key absent leaves the plan unchanged; a re-plan after apply in hub mode with all active is up to date.

cells.title: Switch a project to hub principles in one onboard --skillstation run
cells.action: D9: when `opts.skillstation` and the Claude runtime is in scope, onboard treats the project as hub mode even when skillstation.principles is not hub yet. Plan: (a) when the tracked .bee/config.json does not set skillstation.principles to hub, one item `set_principles_hub` (path .bee/config.json) that apply runs by setting the key to the string hub, keeping every other key, through the existing config write helper; (b) the principle publish items as today; (c) for every local `.claude/skills/bee-principle-*` folder that the hub check does not already remove, a `remove_skill` item carrying `"after_publish": true`. Tests with set_test_hub: --skillstation on a local-mode project plans set_principles_hub, publish items and after_publish removals; apply with every publish succeeding writes hub to config and removes .claude/skills principle folders but keeps .agents ones; apply with one failing publish keeps all and reports one skip row; a plan without --skillstation after a successful switch is up_to_date with the hub reporting every principle active.

Then fix (D11): when the --skillstation switch is active, plan the Claude agent file items as hub-mode renders (give compute_agent_file_plan / render_claude_agent_file an explicit hub override instead of the config read only), mark them `after_publish`, and make apply run `set_principles_hub` before any other after_publish item, and the agent items after it, so apply's re-render reads hub. When a principle publish failed, the agent items do not run. Also add a test: one failing principle publish leaves the agent files local and the config unchanged.
